title: De transformatione serierum in fractiones continuas, ubi simul haec theoria non mediocriter amplificatur

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues Euler's programme of turning power series, and series of reciprocal products, into continued fractions.

(1) It first finishes the example begun on p.159. Theorem IV gives the continued fraction for x/arctan-type series with α,β,γ,... = 1,3,5,7,... and x=1, y=3. Since arctan(1/√3)=π/6, this yields
6√3/π = 3 + 1·3/(8 + 3·9/(12 + 3·25/(16 + ...))).
The general term is (2k−1)²·3 over 4(k+1). Numerically the truncation gives about 3.312 against the true value 3.30797, so it is consistent.

(2) §37 generalises Theorem IV by replacing α,β,γ,... with α/a, β/b, γ/c, .... The series becomes s = Σ(−1)^{n−1} a_n x^n /(α_n y^n). Euler then clears the inner fractions by an equivalence transformation:
- multiply the whole equation by a;
- multiply the k-th partial numerator and denominator by the product of consecutive letters (ab, bc, cd, ...).
This gives Theorem V (§38):
ax/s = αy + α²bxy/(aβy − αbx + β²acxy/(bγy − cβx + γ²bdxy/(cδy − dγx + ...))).

(3) Problem III / §39 converts s = 1/α − 1/(αβ) + 1/(αβγ) − ... into a continued fraction.
- The tails t, u, ... satisfy s=(1−t)/α, t=(1−u)/β, ....
- Hence 1/s = α/(1−t) = α + α/(−1 + 1/t).
- Iterating, carried over to the next page, gives Theorem VI: 1/s = α + α/(β−1 + β/(γ−1 + ...)).
- This is applied there to e: e/(e−1) = 1 + 1/(1 + 2/(2 + 3/(3 + ...))).

The whole page is a rescaling/specialisation of Euler's series-to-continued-fraction correspondence (the 'Euler continued fraction formula').
errors: No mathematical errors found. The equivalence-transformation multipliers ab, bc, cd, ... check out term by term: partial numerators α²b, β²ac, γ²bd and denominators aβy−αbx, bγy−cβx, cδy−dγx.
The numerical example 6√3/π = 3 + 3/(8+27/(12+75/(16+...))) is consistent with 6√3/π ≈ 3.30797.

ideas.what: Insertion of free weights a,b,c,... into the series and clearing nested fractions by multiplying numerator and denominator by consecutive products

ideas.modern_name: Euler's continued fraction formula (series of reciprocal partial products)
ideas.where_published: E123 'De fractionibus continuis observationes' and this paper E593

deep.surprise_reason: Routine specialisations and rescalings of Euler's well-known series-to-continued-fraction formula. The 6√3/π example and Theorems V and VI are standard and documented in Euler's continued-fraction corpus.
transcription_corrections: The left side of the first displayed formula should be 6√3/π, not '4√2/π'. This follows from x=1, y=3 in the √(xy)/A tang √(x/y) formula, and the previous page ends with '6√3'.
The partial numerators read 1·3, 3·9, 3·25 (i.e. xy=3 times 1, 9, 25), consistent with the image. The question marks in the transcription can be removed.
